date.as_written: samvat 786 caitrakṛ trayodaśī pra caturdaśyān tithau revatī pra aśvinī nakṣatra ādityavāra

notes: The Newari '(tho kuhnū dhunakājuro)' means 'finished on this day' (tho kunhu dhunakā juro), so the date is the completion date. The name and role are inside the cataloguer's [[ ]] brackets: '[[śrīharivaṃśanāthavatacocaka || ]]'. This passage may be in a later hand or a doubtful reading, so it is uncertain whether it belongs to the original colophon. The segmentation of the name is unclear. 'vata' might be a corrupt case ending or particle (Newari ergative -na/-naṃ?), or it might be part of the name. 'cocaka' is probably a corrupt Newari verb from coy- ('to write'). If it stands for coyā ('wrote'), Harivaṃśanātha is the scribe. If it stands for coyakā ('had written'), he is the commissioner. The scribe role is tentative. Date: no era is given, but 'samvat 786' in Newari script is taken as NS, so 786 + 880 gives about 1666 CE (Caitra kṛṣṇa, around March/April 1666). The weekday and nakṣatra have not been checked against an ephemeris.
